finding: page-wide getByRole('listbox').first() resolves to an always-visible inline gallery panel, not the opened overlay: the select/combobox cases assert nothing and then hang on the hidden-wait
multiselect and popover have not executed since c1a7c82a5 — the select hang consumes the test budget before the loop reaches them, so two overlay cases silently have zero coverage
locator.waitFor has no default timeout, so the best-effort .catch(() => undefined) on the close wait is unreachable and a stuck overlay burns the whole 60s budget, misreporting against the next case

the #183 regression pin has had no subject since the activity rail landed (cf5ef5fe2 / 3dba5f735): the fixture's three cards all became rail rows, so the spec asserts 0 >= 3 and the shipped CollapsibleBlock inset is unprotected
the coverage reason claims ThinkingContent's clamped state is pinned by deep-chat-collapsed-tool-boxes; that surface renders no ThinkingContent at all since the rail took over 'thinking'

reads a mutable extension registry while memo'd on props that never change when an extension registers, so a block rendered first shows 'Unknown content type: <type>' permanently — measured 1 bad load in 14 on the elicitation surfaces, i.e. a blocking request for user input rendering as debug text

same defect one level up: rail segmentation calls resolveRailStep unsubscribed, so a message segmented before the rail contributions register renders raw tool cards and never shows the activity rail — reproduced 16/16 under concurrent load

isEdgePainted measures then screenshots using coordinates read several awaits earlier; a scroll in between makes both strips sample background and reports 'LEFT border is not painted (issue #183)' for a ring that is present
openSurface waited on the clamp, not on the cards; the cards mount later (lazy extension import), so the spec measured a turn that had not finished growing
the flush-at-top precondition (<=4px) can no longer be met by any inline card type on an assistant turn; the bound was raised to the measured 12px and the lost coverage named rather than hidden

first repair attempt mutated the scroll position inside its own waitForFunction predicate; it fought the app's own scrolling and never converged, turning four passing tests into 60s timeouts. Replaced with read-only quiet-detection plus a bounded retry.
